**Supported facts**

To make `Bun.WebView` connect to an already-running browser over a CDP WebSocket, Bun documents the `backend` object form with `type: "chrome"` and a `url` field set to a `ws://...` DevTools endpoint; the example shown is `ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/abc123...`. The docs say this is how to “Connect to a specific DevTools WebSocket URL.”  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

Bun also documents an auto-connect path: before spawning Chrome, it checks `DevToolsActivePort` in standard profile directories, and if it finds a running browser with remote debugging enabled, it connects over WebSocket instead of spawning a new browser.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

To enable that remote debugging on a running Chrome, the docs say to either use `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` and enable the toggle, or launch Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

The docs state that `url: false` disables auto-detect and forces Bun to spawn a fresh headless Chrome instead. They also state that an explicit `url: "ws://..."` does **not** fall back to spawning if the connection fails; instead, it throws.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

The docs further state that `path` or `argv` imply spawn mode, skip auto-detect, and cannot be combined with `url: "ws://..."`.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

**Documented lifecycle operations**

The explicitly documented lifecycle operations are `view.close()` and `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

For `view.close()`, the docs say closing is synchronous and idempotent, destroys the page’s renderer process, rejects pending promises on that view with `Error("WebView closed")`, and makes later method calls throw `ERR_INVALID_STATE`. They also say `Symbol.dispose` and `Symbol.asyncDispose` both point to `close()`, so `using` and `await using` perform automatic cleanup.

**Supported facts**

To make `Bun.WebView` connect to an already-running browser over a CDP WebSocket, Bun documents the `backend` object form with `type: "chrome"` and a `url` field set to a `ws://...` DevTools endpoint; the example shown is `ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/abc123...`. The docs say this is how to “Connect to a specific DevTools WebSocket URL.”  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

Bun also documents an auto-connect path: before spawning Chrome, it checks `DevToolsActivePort` in standard profile directories, and if it finds a running browser with remote debugging enabled, it connects over WebSocket instead of spawning a new browser.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

To enable that remote debugging on a running Chrome, the docs say to either use `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` and enable the toggle, or launch Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

The docs state that `url: false` disables auto-detect and forces Bun to spawn a fresh headless Chrome instead. They also state that an explicit `url: "ws://..."` does **not** fall back to spawning if the connection fails; instead, it throws.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

The docs further state that `path` or `argv` imply spawn mode, skip auto-detect, and cannot be combined with `url: "ws://..."`.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

**Documented lifecycle operations**

The explicitly documented lifecycle operations are `view.close()` and `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

For `view.close()`, the docs say closing is synchronous and idempotent, destroys the page’s renderer process, rejects pending promises on that view with `Error("WebView closed")`, and makes later method calls throw `ERR_INVALID_STATE`. They also say `Symbol.dispose` and `Symbol.asyncDispose` both point to `close()`, so `using` and `await using` perform automatic cleanup.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

For `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`, the docs say it force-kills the Chrome subprocess and the WebKit host subprocess with `SIGKILL`, causes pending promises on every view to reject on the next event-loop tick, and allows later `new Bun.WebView()` calls to respawn browsers as needed. The docs also say Bun calls `closeAll()` automatically at process exit.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

The same lifecycle section also documents behavior, not separate operations: browser subprocesses do not keep Bun’s event loop alive by themselves, and if the subprocess dies unexpectedly, pending promises reject and further operations on affected views throw.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

**Inference**

The example URL path `/devtools/browser/...` is evidence that Bun expects a **browser-level** CDP WebSocket endpoint, but the docs do not literally define “browser-level” in those words in the `backend.url` option table. That label is an inference from the example and the surrounding text.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

**Disagreement / uncertainty**

There is a small wording mismatch in the docs: the auto-detect text refers to a “Chrome-family browser,” while the `backend.url` reference says `url` is the `ws://` URL of an existing Chrome’s DevTools endpoint. The page does not clearly state whether an explicit `url` is supported for every Chrome-family browser named elsewhere on the page or only for Chrome-compatible DevTools endpoints generally.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

**Lack of good evidence**

I did not find current official Bun documentation on that page specifying support for a non-`ws://` scheme, a tab-level `devtools/page/...` URL, authentication on the WebSocket URL, or any lifecycle operation beyond `close()` and `closeAll()`.  
Source: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview

# Chrome Backend & Lifecycle Information

## Connecting to an Existing Browser

Regarding auto-detection: "By default, before spawning, Bun reads the `DevToolsActivePort` file from standard profile directories to check whether a Chrome-family browser is **already running**" with remote debugging enabled.

To enable this feature, users should "visit `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` and flip the toggle, or launch Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`."

For explicit control, developers can use the object form: `backend: { type: "chrome", url: false }` to skip auto-detect, or provide a specific WebSocket URL like `url: "ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/abc123..."`.

The documentation notes: "If auto-detect finds a stale `DevToolsActivePort` file (Chrome crashed or restarted), the WebSocket connect fails and Bun transparently falls back to spawning its own Chrome."

## Lifecycle Management

Key lifecycle methods include:

- `close()` — "Closing is synchronous and idempotent. It destroys the page's renderer process, rejects any pending promises on the view"
- `Bun.WebView.closeAll()` — "Force-kills (`SIGKILL`) both the Chrome subprocess and the WebKit host subprocess"

The documentation emphasizes: "Bun calls this automatically at process exit, so browser subprocesses never outlive your script."

Regarding automatic cleanup, the `using` keyword works because "`Bun.WebView` implements `Symbol.dispose` and `Symbol.asyncDispose`."

## Réponse

### 1. Connexion à un navigateur déjà lancé via une URL WebSocket CDP de niveau navigateur

**Fait documenté.** `Bun.WebView` accepte une option de constructeur `backend`, qui peut prendre une forme objet permettant de pointer explicitement vers une URL WebSocket DevTools ([bun.com/docs/runtime/webview](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview)) :

```js
using view = new Bun.WebView({
  backend: {
    type: "chrome",
    url: "ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/abc123...",
  },
});
```

La doc décrit ce champ comme servant à « Connect to a specific DevTools WebSocket URL ». Il s'agit bien d'un *endpoint de niveau navigateur* (chemin `/devtools/browser/<id>`), et non d'une cible page.

**Fait documenté — détection automatique.** Par défaut, il n'est pas nécessaire de fournir cette URL : « By default, before spawning, Bun reads the `DevToolsActivePort` file from standard profile directories to check whether a Chrome-family browser is already running » avec le débogage distant activé ; le cas échéant, Bun s'y connecte par WebSocket au lieu de lancer son propre processus, et les vues s'ouvrent comme onglets du navigateur existant ([doc](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview)).

**Fait documenté — activation côté navigateur.** Pour rendre un Chrome existant détectable/connectable : « visit `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` and flip the toggle, or launch Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` » ([doc](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview)).

**Fait documenté — désactivation et repli.** `backend: { type: "chrome", url: false }` désactive l'auto-détection. Et : « If auto-detect finds a stale `DevToolsActivePort` file (Chrome crashed or restarted), the WebSocket connect fails and Bun transparently falls back to spawning its own Chrome » ([doc](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview)).

**Portée de la plateforme.** Ce chemin CDP concerne Linux et Windows, où Bun pilote un Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave installé via le Chrome DevTools Protocol ; sur macOS, le backend par défaut est `WKWebView` du système ([doc](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview)).

**Commandes CDP brutes.** Une fois connecté, `view.cdp(...)` permet d'envoyer des commandes CDP directement, p. ex. `view.cdp("DOM.getDocument")` ([référence `WebView.cdp`](https://bun.com/reference/bun/WebView/cdp)).

### 2. Opérations de cycle de vie documentées

D'après la [documentation officielle](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview) et la [référence API](https://bun.com/reference/bun/WebView) :

| Opération | Statut |
|---|---|
| `navigate(url)` | documentée |
| `reload()` | documentée |
| `goBack()` / `goForward()` | documentées |
| `close()` | documentée : « Closing is synchronous and idempotent. It destroys the page's renderer process, rejects any pending promises on the view » |
| `Symbol.dispose` / `Symbol.asyncDispose` | documentés : `using` / `await using` ferment la vue en sortie de portée |
| `Bun.WebView.closeAll()` (statique) | documentée : « Force-kills (`SIGKILL`) both the Chrome subprocess and the WebKit host subprocess » ; « Bun calls this automatically at process exit, so browser subprocesses never outlive your script » |

Propriétés/callbacks liés au cycle de vie : `url`, `title`, `loading` (lecture seule), `onNavigated`, `onNavigationFailed` ([doc](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview)).

Autres options du constructeur : `width`, `height`, `url`, `headless`, `backend`, `console`, `dataStore` ([référence](https://bun.com/reference/bun/WebView)).

### 3. Réserves, incertitudes et limites de preuve

- **Statut expérimental (fait).** La doc qualifie `Bun.WebView` d'expérimental, l'API pouvant évoluer ([doc](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/webview)) — donc tout ce qui précède est daté du jour.
- **Ambiguïté de nommage (fait, à souligner).** `url` existe à deux niveaux différents : au niveau du constructeur c'est l'URL de page initiale, au niveau de `backend` c'est l'endpoint WebSocket CDP. Ne pas les confondre.
- **Incertitude — sémantique de `close()` sur un navigateur *attaché*.** Je n'ai pas trouvé de texte officiel précisant si `close()`/`closeAll()` se comporte différemment quand Bun s'est *connecté* à un navigateur préexistant plutôt que de l'avoir lancé lui-même. La formulation de `closeAll()` (« force-kills the Chrome subprocess ») suggère un processus enfant de Bun ; **il s'agit d'une inférence**, non d'un fait établi. Prudence si vous attachez Bun à votre navigateur de travail quotidien.
- **Preuve partielle sur la page de référence.** La page [bun.com/reference/bun/WebView](https://bun.com/reference/bun/WebView) que j'ai pu récupérer exposait surtout les interfaces et options du constructeur ; les méthodes de cycle de vie y étaient listées par sous-pages (p. ex. [`WebView/click`](https://bun.com/reference/bun/WebView/click), [`WebView/cdp`](https://bun.com/reference/bun/WebView/cdp)). La page de type `WebView.Backend` que j'ai tentée renvoie 404, donc **je n'ai pas de signature TypeScript exacte** du champ `backend` (types acceptés pour `url` au-delà de `string | false`, présence éventuelle d'un champ `port` ou `executable`). Traitez la forme exacte du type comme non vérifiée.
- **Sources tierces écartées.** Des articles de blog/Substack décrivent la même fonctionnalité, mais je ne les ai pas utilisés comme base factuelle ; aucune contradiction notable entre eux et la doc officielle n'a été relevée.
